description: RS_candidate(SAFE) contains only R-SAFE-001 (Go). No Delay rule exists in RS_candidate(SAFE). Go+Delay conflict cannot occur within SAFE state under the current candidate rule set. If the episode is SAFE, only R-SAFE-001 may fire, producing a single Go advisory.

Both R-CAUTION-001 (marine warning Category 1 → Delay) and R-CAUTION-002 (wave in CAUTION band → Delay) may fire in the same episode if S = CAUTION is driven by both m = advisory AND o in vessel CAUTION band simultaneously. Both rules produce Delay advisories with distinct explanations. Multiple advisories of the same type with different rule_ids and different explanation texts are architecturally valid — the rule engine collects all fired rules and returns all generated advisories. The fisher receives richer information (two reasons for delay).
resolution: COMPATIBLE — no conflict. Two Delay advisories with distinct rationales is an acceptable and informationally richer output than a single Delay advisory.
policy_type: N/A — scientific policy not required; implementation must return all fired advisories

description: All three Delay rules (marine warning + wave + rainfall) may fire simultaneously if all three conditions are simultaneously in CAUTION. Each produces a Delay advisory with a distinct explanation. Three simultaneous Delay advisories are consistent in conclusion type and provide the most complete explanation of why delay is recommended.
resolution: COMPATIBLE — multiple consistent Delay advisories are architecturally valid. Implementation returns all fired advisories.

description: All four Delay rules may fire simultaneously in an extreme CAUTION episode. All produce Delay conclusion type. Compatible — maximum four simultaneous Delay advisories with distinct explanations.
resolution: COMPATIBLE — consistent conclusion types across all four rules.

rules_involved: R-SAFE-001 and any future CAUTION/Delay rule in SAFE state
description: If a Delay rule for SAFE state is added in future (e.g., sub-CAUTION wave condition approaching CAUTION boundary) then Go (R-SAFE-001) and Delay (hypothetical future rule) could fire simultaneously in the same SAFE-state episode. This is the Go+Delay conflict the task requires pre-emptive analysis of. Under current RS_candidate(SAFE): NOT POSSIBLE. Under any future RS(SAFE) containing both Go and Delay rules: ADVISORY_CONFLICT_POLICY_REQUIRED.
resolution: Current RS_candidate: no conflict. Future: ADVISORY_CONFLICT_POLICY_REQUIRED — whether Go and Delay can fire simultaneously and how to present conflicting advisories requires a scientific or implementation policy decision. Record as a boundary condition for future rule specification.
policy_type: Scientific policy — which advisory takes precedence or whether both should be reported would require a scientific decision about how to convey conflicting signals to the fisher. An implementation priority rule alone is not sufficient.
requires_action: NO — current candidate set is conflict-free; action needed if future rules create Go+Delay within same state

description: Go advisory in SAFE state (R-SAFE-001) and Delay advisories in CAUTION state (R-CAUTION-001 through R-CAUTION-004) cannot fire in the same episode. Each episode has exactly one S value. RS(SAFE) is used when S = SAFE; RS(CAUTION) is used when S = CAUTION. The one-episode-one-RS invariant (from Batch 1 ReasoningEpisode specification) ensures rule sets from different states never mix.
resolution: NOT APPLICABLE — architectural invariant prevents cross-state rule firing.

description: If additional Go rules are added to RS_candidate(SAFE) with different specific antecedents (e.g., sub-ranges within SAFE) multiple Go advisories could fire. Multiple Go advisories with distinct rule_ids and rationales are architecturally valid but may confuse presentation.
resolution: COMPATIBLE with clarification: presentation layer should aggregate multiple same-type advisories clearly. Not a scientific conflict.
policy_type: Implementation policy — presentation aggregation of multiple same-type advisories
